title: Chatbots replacing customer service staff
prompt:
Many companies now use automated systems, such as chatbots, instead of human staff to answer customers' questions and complaints.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
tips: This question asks for a judgement. Do not just list advantages and disadvantages; say clearly which side is stronger and why.
Consider different stakeholders: companies, customers, and the employees who may lose their jobs.
A good way to show weighing is to explain why one disadvantage matters more (or less) than one advantage.

samples.text:
Nowadays, a lot of companies use chatbots to answer questions from customers instead of people. This has some advantages and disadvantages. In my opinion, the disadvantages are more than the advantages.

There are some advantages of using chatbots. Firstly, chatbots can work 24 hours a day and they never get tired. So customers can ask a question at any time, for example at night or on holidays. Secondly, it is cheaper for the companies because they don't need to pay salary to many workers. They can use the money for other things like make the products better. Also chatbots can answer many customers in the same time, so nobody has to wait on the phone for a long time.

However, there are also many disadvantages. The main disadvantage is that chatbots can't understand difficult problems. For example, last year I had a problem with my bank account and the chatbot only gave me the same answers again and again. I was very angry and I wanted to talk to a real person but it was very difficult. Another disadvantage is that many people will lose their jobs. Customer service is a big job for many young people and if companies use chatbots, these people will be unemployed. It is difficult for them to find a new job quickly.

In conclusion, chatbots are fast and cheap but they can't solve difficult problems and they cause unemployment. So I think the disadvantages outweigh the advantages and companies should still have human staff.
samples.commentary: Task Response: the question is answered with a clear position and relevant points, and the personal example is useful, but the response mainly lists points and does not really weigh them against each other. Coherence and Cohesion: clear paragraphing, though linking is mechanical ('Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Another disadvantage'). Lexical Resource: adequate, with some topic vocabulary ('unemployed', 'customer service'), but repetition ('problem', 'disadvantage') and errors such as 'the disadvantages are more than the advantages' and 'pay salary'. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: a mix of simple and complex sentences with some errors ('like make the products better'), though meaning remains clear. Band 6.

samples.text:
Automated customer service, particularly in the form of chatbots, has become common in industries ranging from banking to online retail. Although this technology offers clear benefits, I believe its drawbacks currently outweigh them.

The main advantage for businesses is cost. A single chatbot can handle thousands of conversations at once, which allows companies to reduce staffing costs significantly. Customers also benefit from instant responses at any time of day, rather than waiting on hold for a human agent. For routine questions, such as checking an order status or resetting a password, an automated system is often faster and perfectly adequate.

However, the limitations of chatbots become obvious when a customer's problem is complex or unusual. Most systems rely on pre-set answers and can trap users in frustrating loops when their question does not fit a category. This is especially damaging when people are already upset, for example when disputing a charge on their bank account. In such situations, being unable to reach a person can seriously damage a customer's trust in the company. There is also a social cost, as customer service has traditionally provided employment for many people without specialist qualifications.

On balance, I think these disadvantages are more significant. The savings that companies make are real, but they may be lost if frustrated customers move to competitors. Moreover, the convenience of chatbots only applies to simple questions, while their failures affect precisely the customers who need help most.

In conclusion, chatbots are useful for straightforward enquiries, but replacing human staff entirely is a mistake. Companies should use automation to support their employees, not to remove them.
samples.commentary: Task Response: a clear position is presented and supported, and there is genuine weighing of the arguments in the fourth paragraph, although the employment point could be developed further. Coherence and Cohesion: well organised with clear progression; cohesive devices are varied and appropriate ('However', 'On balance', 'Moreover'). Lexical Resource: a good range of topic vocabulary ('staffing costs', 'pre-set answers', 'frustrating loops', 'disputing a charge'), with natural collocation. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: complex sentences with relative clauses, participle phrases and gerund subjects are used accurately, with only minor slips. Band 7.

samples.text:
Chatbots have rapidly become the first point of contact between many companies and their customers, replacing the human voice at the end of a phone line with a text box that replies instantly. Whether this shift is beneficial depends largely on how the technology is used, but I would argue that, as it is currently deployed by many firms, its disadvantages outweigh its advantages.

The appeal of automation is easy to understand. For businesses, a single system that can manage thousands of simultaneous conversations offers enormous savings compared with large call centres. For customers, the absence of queues and the availability of help at three in the morning are genuine improvements, and for simple tasks such as tracking a parcel, few people would miss a human operator.

The difficulty is that customer service is rarely judged by how it handles simple tasks. Its real test comes when something has gone wrong: a duplicated payment, a cancelled flight, a faulty product. These cases are often too complex or emotionally charged for scripted responses, and customers who find themselves repeatedly redirected to irrelevant help pages experience the service not as efficient but as obstructive. A company that saves money on staff but loses loyal customers through such encounters has made a poor trade. There is, moreover, a wider social cost, since customer service roles have long been an accessible entry point into employment.

None of this means that chatbots should be abandoned. Used to filter routine questions while passing more complicated cases quickly to trained staff, they could improve service for everyone. The problem lies in treating them as a replacement for people rather than as a tool for them.

Overall, therefore, the benefits of automated customer service are outweighed by its drawbacks unless human help remains easy to reach.
samples.commentary: Task Response: the question is addressed fully with a well-developed, nuanced position; the essay explicitly evaluates why the disadvantages carry more weight, and the conditional conclusion is consistent with the argument. Coherence and Cohesion: skilful paragraphing and sequencing, with cohesion achieved through reference and argument structure ('The difficulty is that', 'None of this means'). Lexical Resource: wide and precise ('first point of contact', 'emotionally charged', 'obstructive', 'accessible entry point'), used naturally and with flexibility. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: a wide range of structures, including cleft-like sentences, reduced relatives and participle clauses, with full control. Band 8.
